```{r}
missing_files <- required_files[!file.exists(required_files)]
if (length(missing_files) > 0) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "The following analysis outputs are missing:\n",

read_table <- function(filename) {
  readr::read_csv(file.path(tables_dir, filename), show_col_types = FALSE)
}

read_main_table <- function(filename) {
  readr::read_csv(file.path(main_tables_dir, filename), show_col_types = FALSE)
}

read_repeatability <- function(filename) {
  readr::read_csv(file.path(repeatability_dir, filename), show_col_types = FALSE)
}

p_text <- function(p, digits = 3) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(p) ~ "—",
    p < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
    TRUE ~ sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), p)
  )
}

range_text <- function(x, digits = 3) {
  sprintf(
    paste0("%.", digits, "f–%.", digits, "f"),
    min(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

supplementary_table <- function(x, align = NULL, font_size = 8.5) {
  x <- as.data.frame(x)
  rule <- officer::fp_border(color = "#000000", width = 0.75)

  ft <- flextable::flextable(x) |>
    flextable::font(fontname = "Times New Roman", part = "all") |>
    flextable::fontsize(size = font_size, part = "all") |>
    flextable::color(color = "#000000", part = "all") |>
    flextable::bold(part = "header") |>
    flextable::border_remove() |>
    flextable::hline_top(border = rule, part = "header") |>
    flextable::hline_bottom(border = rule, part = "header") |>
    flextable::padding(padding = 2, part = "all") |>
    flextable::valign(valign = "center", part = "all") |>
    flextable::autofit() |>
    flextable::set_table_properties(
      layout = "autofit",
      width = 1,
      opts_word = list(split = FALSE, repeat_headers = TRUE)
    )

  if (!is.null(align)) {
    for (j in seq_along(align)) {
      ft <- flextable::align(ft, j = j, align = align[[j]], part = "all")
    }
  }

  ft
}

# Measurement reliability -----------------------------------------------------
repeatability_all <- read_repeatability("measurement_repeatability_robustness.csv")
round_effects     <- read_repeatability("measurement_round_effects.csv")
round_pairwise    <- read_repeatability("measurement_round_pairwise_diagnostics.csv")
order_effects     <- read_repeatability("measurement_order_effects.csv")

repeatability_primary <- repeatability_all |>
  filter(model == "primary_unadjusted")
repeatability_morph <- repeatability_all |>
  filter(model == "morph_adjusted")
repeatability_round <- repeatability_all |>
  filter(model == "morph_and_round_adjusted")

trait_labels <- c(
  pronotum = "Pronotum length",
  head_length = "Head length",
  head_width = "Head width",
  forefemur = "Forefemur length",
  foretibia = "Foretibia length",
  midfemur = "Midfemur length",
  midtibia = "Midtibia length",
  hindfemur = "Hindfemur length",
  hindtibia = "Hindtibia length",
  ear = "Ear area",
  eye = "Eye length"
)

trait_order <- names(trait_labels)

repeatability_display <- repeatability_primary |>
  select(trait, pooled_R = R, pooled_lower = CI_lower, pooled_upper = CI_upper) |>
  left_join(
    repeatability_morph |>
      select(trait, morph_R = R, morph_lower = CI_lower, morph_upper = CI_upper),
    by = "trait"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    repeatability_round |>
      select(
        trait,
        round_R = R,
        round_lower = CI_lower,
        round_upper = CI_upper
      ),
    by = "trait"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    round_effects |>
      select(
        trait,
        relative_TEM_percent,
        absolute_agreement_ICC_A1,
        max_absolute_pairwise_bias_percent,
        round_P_Holm
      ),
    by = "trait"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    trait = factor(trait, levels = trait_order),
    Trait = unname(trait_labels[as.character(trait)]),
    Pooled = sprintf("%.4f\n(%.4f–%.4f)", pooled_R, pooled_lower, pooled_upper),
    `Morph-adjusted` = sprintf(
      "%.4f\n(%.4f–%.4f)", morph_R, morph_lower, morph_upper
    ),
    `Morph + round` = sprintf(
      "%.4f\n(%.4f–%.4f)", round_R, round_lower, round_upper
    ),
    `rTEM (%)` = sprintf("%.2f", relative_TEM_percent),
    `ICC(A,1)` = sprintf("%.4f", absolute_agreement_ICC_A1),
    `Max. bias (%)` = sprintf("%.2f", max_absolute_pairwise_bias_percent),
    `Holm p` = p_text(round_P_Holm)
  ) |>
  arrange(trait) |>
  select(
    Trait,
    Pooled,
    `Morph-adjusted`,
    `Morph + round`,
    `rTEM (%)`,
    `ICC(A,1)`,
    `Max. bias (%)`,
    `Holm p`
  )

min_signed_order_q   <- min(order_effects$signed_slope_P_BH, na.rm = TRUE)
min_absolute_order_q <- min(order_effects$absolute_error_slope_P_BH, na.rm = TRUE)

# Dimensionality sensitivities ------------------------------------------------

dimensionality_display <- bind_rows(

    transmute(
      Approach = "Female-referenced rank-one test",

        scenario,
        standardized_head_excluded = "Five traits, standardized; head excluded (base scenario)",

        raw_log_six = "Six traits on raw log scale"

    pca_primary |> mutate(Scenario = "Five traits, standardized; head excluded (base scenario)"),
    pca_six |> mutate(Scenario = "Six traits, standardized; head included"),

      mutate(Scenario = "Five traits after excluding classification-sensitive males")
  ) |>
    transmute(

        "PC1 = %.1f%%; eigenvalue %.3f",
        variance_percent,
        observed_eigenvalue
      ),
      `Null reference` = sprintf(
        "95th-percentile eigenvalue = %.3f",

      ),
      `p-value` = "—",

      Estimate = predicted_ear_area,
      `Lower 95% CI` = ear_area_lower,
      `Upper 95% CI` = ear_area_upper
    ),
  eye_means_main |>
    transmute(
      Trait = "Eye length (mm)", Group = group,
      Estimate = predicted_eye_length,
      `Lower 95% CI` = eye_lower,
      `Upper 95% CI` = eye_upper
    )
) |>
  mutate(across(c(Estimate, `Lower 95% CI`, `Upper 95% CI`), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

# Overview

This supplement distinguishes detailed estimates from the main-text models (Tables S14–S17) from additional analyses (Tables S1–S13 and Figures S1–S4). The latter include measurement reliability, multivariate descriptions, covariance-matrix comparisons, alternative weapon–trait specifications, classification and sample-composition checks, equivalence-region sensitivities and a cross-analysis multiplicity audit. Both documents use the same `analysis_outputs` results, generated by `scripts/run_all.R` and its separate repeatability script. Analyses not used for main-text inference are explicitly identified as exploratory or sensitivity analyses rather than presented as additional primary tests.

Residual-index models, separate segment-level decompositions and extensive group-specific slope searches are retained in the reproducibility archive but are not promoted as inferential evidence. They either duplicate a one-stage model reported here or do not materially change the biological conclusions.

# Supplementary methods

## Measurement reliability

Forty-eight specimens from the 2016 collection were measured on three occasions. The measurement-order file records 12 individuals per sex or morph group and one from each of 12 size strata within each group. Repeatability was estimated for pooled, morph-adjusted and morph-plus-round models. Relative technical error of measurement, absolute-agreement ICC(A,1), round-pair bias and measurement-order trends were also calculated. The order analyses were treated as diagnostics; their minimum Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted p-values were `r p_text(min_signed_order_q)` for signed drift and `r p_text(min_absolute_order_q)` for absolute-error drift.

## Multivariate sensitivity analyses

The base female-referenced contrast-vector and PCA analyses excluded composite head size because head length contributed to male morph assignment. Sensitivity analyses restored head size, repeated the rank-one decomposition on unstandardized log traits, and repeated the five-trait PCA after excluding males whose archived labels disagreed with the published 2010 head-length thresholds. These multivariate analyses are supplementary explorations, not tests reported as primary in the accompanying manuscript. The permutation analyses used 9,999 permutations.

## Matrix comparisons and unequal sample sizes

Within-group covariance and correlation matrices for the five non-head traits were compared using omnibus and pairwise Frobenius-distance randomization tests. Pairwise p-values were adjusted by both Benjamini–Hochberg and Holm procedures. Matrix-element correlations and random-skewers similarities were used as descriptive orientation measures. To evaluate unequal group sizes, each group was repeatedly rarefied to 38 specimens, the size of the tenth-instar male group.

## Repeated-leg covariance structure

The main repeated-leg model estimated separate residual variances for fore-, mid- and hindlegs and freely estimated the three within-individual residual correlations. It was compared with compound-symmetry and heterogeneous compound-symmetry structures using fits with identical fixed effects. An earlier random-intercept model, which assumed a more restrictive covariance structure, gave a different conclusion for the body-size-by-group-by-leg interaction; the revised unstructured model is used for main-text inference. A separate individual-by-leg random intercept is not identifiable because each individual-by-leg cell contains one observation.

## Secondary integration, equivalence and sampling checks

Main-text weapon–leg relationships were estimated in one stage from raw log composite head size while controlling for pronotum length, group and leg identity. Weapon–ear slopes were likewise estimated in one stage; an exploratory equivalence sensitivity assessed them against an illustrative standardized near-zero region of −0.20 to 0.20. All-pairs sensory comparisons were Holm-adjusted within each six-comparison trait family and are separate from the main text's planned contrast families. Morph-composition χ² tests compared the analysed males with two published empirical compositions; they diagnose compositional mismatch but cannot identify its cause because collection microhabitat and gallery-search effort were not retained.

## Cross-analysis multiplicity audit

The within-family Holm adjustments reported for planned contrasts remain the manuscript's inferential corrections. As a separate sensitivity analysis, ten selected omnibus p-values were adjusted together using Benjamini–Hochberg and Holm procedures. This broader audit is descriptive and does not replace the main-text tests.

# Supplementary results

## Reliability and measurement-session effects

All traits were highly repeatable, and the conclusions were unchanged after adjustment for morph and measurement round (Table S1). Round effects were detectable for several traits, but their magnitude was small relative to among-individual variation. No evidence of progressive signed or absolute-error drift was detected within remeasurement sessions.

## Directional dimensionality

The base five-trait rank-one model captured `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * rank_primary$rank_one_fraction)`% of design-weighted group-effect variation, while the standardized six-trait and raw-log six-trait sensitivities captured `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * rank_six$rank_one_fraction)`% and `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * rank_raw$rank_one_fraction)`%, respectively. In every case the residual component beyond rank one exceeded the randomization distribution (`r p_text(max(rank_one$p_value))`; Table S7). Parallel analysis retained one component in the base five-trait analysis, the six-trait sensitivity and the classification-exclusion sensitivity (Supplementary Figure S2). These exploratory results show one dominant dimension together with a smaller detected secondary direction in adjusted group means.

## Matrix structure

The base five-trait omnibus tests detected neither a covariance-matrix difference (`r p_text(primary_covariance$p_value)`) nor a correlation-matrix difference (`r p_text(primary_correlation$p_value)`; Supplementary Figure S1). The six-trait sensitivity detected a covariance-magnitude difference (`r p_text(six_covariance$p_value)`), but not a correlation-matrix difference (`r p_text(six_correlation$p_value)`). No five-trait pairwise matrix comparison survived Holm adjustment (Table S8). Matrix-element correlations, random-skewers similarities and rarefaction summaries are reported in Table S9 rather than interpreted as independent hypothesis tests.

## Repeated-leg covariance and secondary analyses

In the alternative covariance-structure fits, unstructured repeated-leg covariance was preferred to heterogeneous compound symmetry (likelihood-ratio statistic = `r sprintf("%.2f", leg_covariance_selected$L.Ratio)`, `r p_text(leg_covariance_selected_p)`; Table S10a). Pairwise residual correlations ranged from `r sprintf("%.3f", min(leg_covariance_parameters$estimate[1:3]))` to `r sprintf("%.3f", max(leg_covariance_parameters$estimate[1:3]))` (Table S10b). The one-stage raw-head weapon–leg slopes were positive in 11 of 12 group-by-leg combinations, but planned differences among slopes were imprecise (Tables S3–S4). Weapon–ear slopes did not meet the illustrative equivalence criterion in any group (Table S5).

## Classification and sample composition

The archived file contained `r morph_classification$male_n` males. Applying the published 2010 thresholds changed `r morph_classification$n_disagree_legacy_2010` labels (`r sprintf("%.1f", morph_classification$percent_disagree_legacy_2010)`%). Excluding those specimens did not alter the head-adjusted eye-length omnibus conclusion (Table S11). Male composition differed from both published empirical references (Table S11), but the source of the difference cannot be resolved from the archive. The 7.2-mm reference pronotum used for adjusted comparisons fell within the observed range of every group (Supplementary Figure S3).

## Cross-analysis multiplicity

In the selected unstructured model, the group-by-leg allocation effect and the raw-head weapon–leg interaction remained supported in the ten-test audit. The body-size-by-group-by-leg interaction was unsupported even before cross-analysis adjustment (Table S12); the earlier random-intercept model gave a nominal $p=0.044$. The difference is a model-specification sensitivity, not merely an effect of multiplicity adjustment, and warrants caution when interpreting detailed allometric-slope differences.
